senses.gloss: To argue with someone in a lively way that is not really hostile.
examples: The two candidates *spar* over health care in every debate.
She *sparred* with reporters for twenty minutes.
They have been *sparring* about the budget all week.

senses.gloss: To be able to give someone time, money, or attention that you can do without.
examples: Can you *spare* ten minutes to look at this?
She *spared* me a few dollars for the bus.
They are *sparing* no expense on the new lab.

senses.gloss: To let someone go free or unharmed when you could punish or kill them.
examples: They begged the soldiers to *spare* the village.
The judge *spared* him jail time.
Only one building was *spared* by the fire.

senses.gloss: To cause something new to come into existence, especially in large numbers.
examples: One hit movie can *spawn* a dozen imitations.
The scandal *spawned* three separate investigations.
The show has *spawned* two spin-offs and a video game.

senses.gloss: To rise sharply and suddenly.
examples: Gas prices *spike* every summer.
Cases *spiked* after the holiday weekend.
Demand has *spiked* since the storm.

senses.gloss: To add alcohol or a drug to a drink, usually without telling anyone.
examples: Never leave your drink where someone could *spike* it.
Somebody *spiked* the punch at the party.
She is sure her soda was *spiked*.

senses.gloss: To increase or get worse quickly and without control.
senses.ru: стремительно расти, выходить из-под контроля (о ценах, долгах)
examples: Costs can *spiral* if the work is delayed.
Her debts *spiraled* after she lost the job.
Rents have been *spiraling* for three years.

senses.gloss: To break apart into smaller rival groups.
examples: Without a leader, the movement could *splinter*.
The party *splintered* into three factions.
The opposition has *splintered* into rival camps.

senses.gloss: To formally put a bill or a proposal forward in a legislature.
examples: She plans to *sponsor* legislation on clean water.
Two senators *sponsored* the bill last spring.
The measure is *sponsored* by lawmakers from both parties.

senses.gloss: To take formal responsibility for someone so that they can enter a country or join a group.
senses.ru: выступать поручителем, поручиться; оформлять спонсорство (визу, грин-карту)
examples: His employer agreed to *sponsor* his visa.
She *sponsored* her mother for a green card.
He was *sponsored* by an uncle who already lived in Chicago.

senses.gloss: To lend someone a small amount of money.
examples: Can you *spot* me twenty bucks until Friday?
He *spotted* me the cab fare.
She is always *spotting* her roommate lunch money.

senses.gloss: To stand beside someone lifting weights, ready to take the bar if they cannot hold it.
examples: Will you *spot* me on this set?
His friend *spotted* him while he benched.
Nobody was *spotting* her when the bar came down.

senses.gloss: To rain very lightly.
examples: It may *sprinkle* this afternoon, but the game will go on.
It *sprinkled* a little overnight.
It was *sprinkling*, so we took an umbrella.

senses.gloss: To put a stop to something before it can grow, such as a rumor or a protest.
examples: The mayor moved quickly to *squash* the rumor.
Management *squashed* the idea in one meeting.
The revolt was *squashed* within a week.

senses.gloss: To live in an empty building without permission and without paying rent.
examples: Several families *squat* in the old hotel.
He *squatted* in an empty warehouse for two years.
People have been *squatting* in the building since it closed.

senses.gloss: To put someone under financial pressure by leaving them less money.
senses.ru: стеснять в средствах, зажимать; создавать финансовое давление
examples: High rents *squeeze* young families.
The new tariffs *squeezed* small importers.
Farmers are being *squeezed* by low prices and high fuel costs.

senses.gloss: To arrange something so that it looks real or accidental when it is not.
examples: The thieves tried to *stage* a break-in.
He *staged* the accident to collect the insurance.
Every photo in the ad was carefully *staged*.

senses.gloss: To shock or amaze someone.
examples: The repair bill will *stagger* you.
The size of the crowd *staggered* the organizers.
I was *staggered* by how much the house sold for.

senses.gloss: To arrange times so that they do not all happen at once.
senses.ru: разносить по времени, распределять (смены, время начала)
examples: The school will *stagger* start times by half an hour.
They *staggered* the shifts to keep the floor from getting crowded.
Boarding is *staggered* by row.

senses.gloss: To risk money or something valuable on the result of something.
examples: I would not *stake* my savings on a rumor.
He *staked* his reputation on the forecast.
She has *staked* everything on this one deal.

senses.gloss: To walk stiffly and angrily so that everyone notices.
senses.ru: уходить в гневе, гордо шагать, вышагивать со злостью
examples: Don't *stalk* around the house all evening just because you lost.
She *stalked* past me without a word.
He came *stalking* into the meeting twenty minutes late.

senses.gloss: To delay on purpose in order to gain time.
examples: They will *stall* as long as the law allows.
He *stalled* until his lawyer arrived.
Stop *stalling* and answer the question.

senses.gloss: To stop making progress.
examples: Talks between the two sides *stalled* in March.
Sales have *stalled* since the spring.
The project is *stalling* for lack of money.

senses.gloss: To bring your foot down hard on the ground or on something.
examples: Don't *stamp* your feet at me.
She *stamped* on the spider.
He kept *stamping* his boots to knock the snow off.

senses.gloss: To begin doing something, or to begin happening.
examples: The movie *starts* at eight.
She *started* crying before the song ended.
We have already *started* packing.

senses.gloss: To set up a new business, group, or project.
examples: They want to *start* a bakery downtown.
He *started* the company in his garage.
She has *started* a book club at the library.

senses.gloss: To keep a person, a place, or a thing from getting something it badly needs.
senses.ru: лишать необходимого, недофинансировать; морить (голодом, без средств)
examples: Budget cuts *starve* rural clinics of nurses.
The program was *starved* of funding for years.
You are *starving* that plant of light.

senses.gloss: To continue to be in a particular state or condition.
examples: Try to *stay* calm.
The store *stayed* open until midnight.
Prices have *stayed* low all year.

senses.gloss: To live somewhere for a short time as a guest.
examples: We usually *stay* at a motel near the airport.
They *stayed* with my sister for a week.
I have *stayed* in that hotel twice.

senses.gloss: To guide a person or a conversation in a particular direction.
examples: A good teacher can *steer* students toward the right question.
She *steered* the conversation away from money.
He has been *steering* his son toward engineering for years.

senses.gloss: To operate on a person or an animal so that they cannot have young.
examples: The shelter will *sterilize* every animal before adoption.
The vet *sterilized* our cat last spring.
All the dogs here have been *sterilized*.

senses.gloss: To keep worrying or being angry about something instead of doing anything.
examples: Don't *stew* about it all night — just call her.
He *stewed* for days over that email.
She left him *stewing* in the waiting room.

senses.gloss: To make it hard or impossible for someone to breathe.
examples: The smoke began to *stifle* us.
He was *stifled* by the thick dust in the attic.
The heat in that room was *stifling*.

senses.gloss: To make a system or a part of the body more active.
examples: Exercise *stimulates* blood flow to the muscles.
The tax cut *stimulated* hiring for about a year.
The grant money is *stimulating* new research across the state.

senses.gloss: To move slightly, especially after being still or asleep.
examples: Nobody *stirs* in this house before seven.
The baby *stirred* and went back to sleep.
The leaves were *stirring* in the first breeze of the morning.

senses.gloss: To prevent someone from doing something.
examples: Nothing will *stop* her from trying again.
The rain *stopped* us from finishing the roof.
What is *stopping* you from applying?

senses.gloss: To go somewhere in a noisy, angry way.
examples: He tends to *storm* around the kitchen when he is angry.
She *stormed* into the principal's office.
He came *storming* past me without a word.

senses.gloss: To rain, snow, or blow violently.
examples: It is supposed to *storm* tonight.
It *stormed* all weekend, so the game was canceled.
It has been *storming* since dawn.

senses.gloss: To make a great effort, especially to see or hear something.
examples: I had to *strain* to hear the announcement.
She *strained* to see over the crowd.
He was *straining* against the ropes.

senses.gloss: To flow or move steadily in a continuous current.
senses.ru: литься, течь потоком; валить, хлынуть (о толпе)
examples: Light *streams* through that window every morning.
Tears *streamed* down her face.
Fans were *streaming* out of the stadium.

senses.gloss: To spread out over a distance or over a period of time.
examples: The beach *stretches* for eleven miles.
The meeting *stretched* into the evening.
The line was *stretching* around the block by noon.

senses.gloss: To take an official title, right, or position away from someone.
examples: The board can *strip* him of his license.
The court *stripped* her of custody.
He was *stripped* of the gold medal.

senses.gloss: To find something very difficult to do.
senses.ru: с трудом справляться, испытывать трудности; еле справляться
examples: Some students *struggle* with word problems.
She *struggled* to pay rent last winter.
The team has been *struggling* all season.

senses.gloss: To travel around an area making speeches in a political campaign.
senses.ru: вести предвыборную агитацию, разъезжать с выступлениями
examples: He plans to *stump* across Iowa in October.
She *stumped* for her party in six states.
They have been *stumping* in small towns all month.
